_comment: MODEL L (Assamese) pretraining run. Consumed by common/train.py.
_budget: One pass over the full 559,751,349-token training ribbon:
max_steps is left null so train.py computes it from the ribbon; the
numbers above are what it should print. 560M tokens against 24.6M
parameters is roughly 23 tokens per parameter, near the compute
optimal ratio for a model of this size, so a single pass is the right
budget rather than an arbitrary stopping point.
_batch: micro_batch 24 is what a 16 GB T4 holds at block 512: the attention
probabilities alone are 24 x 6 x 512 x 512 per layer and are kept for
the backward pass. grad_accum 5 then builds a 61,440-token gradient,
which is large enough that the loss curve is readable rather than
noisy. Memory decides only how the batch is split, not its size.
If a T4 reports OOM, halve micro_batch and double grad_accum -- the
effective batch, and therefore the run, is unchanged.
_precision: fp16 with a GradScaler, not bf16. The Kaggle T4 is Turing and has no
bfloat16 support at all. fp16's exponent range is narrow enough that
small gradients flush to zero, so the scaler multiplies the loss
before backward and divides it out before the step.
_learning_rate: 6e-4 peak with 400 warmup steps and cosine decay to 6e-5. Warmup
because Adam's second moment is an average over the steps taken so
far, so its first few hundred updates are oversized and land on a
randomly initialised model. 400 steps is ~4.4% of the run.
beta2 0.95 rather than 0.999: at 0.999 the second moment averages
over ~1000 steps, more than a tenth of this entire run.
name: model_l_pretrain
